    #166445. The S&P 500 is in a correction. Bear markets and recessions don't always follow

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (566 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The S&P 500 is in a correction. Bear markets and recessions don't always follow

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov.
    • The market correction, defined as a 10% decline from a recent high, came as investor concern mounted over a potential slowdown in AI spending, mega-cap tech valuations and the path of Federal Reserve interest rate policy.
    • In a recent development, A correction can deepen into a bear market, defined as a drop of 20% or more from the most recent top.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov. 20 for the first time since April 2025 as stocks pulled back sharply from October's record highs.

    The market correction, defined as a 10% decline from a recent high, came as investor concern mounted over a potential slowdown in AI spending, mega-cap tech valuations and the path of Federal Reserve interest rate policy. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Nov. 20 alone, closing at 6,910.39, its seventh consecutive daily decline. That left the index 11.6% below the Oct. 6 closing high of 7,818.93.

    In a recent development, A correction can deepen into a bear market, defined as a drop of 20% or more from the most recent top. But history shows that even a bear market, let alone a correction, doesn't automatically mean the economy is destined for a recession.

    It has been revealed that in a CNBC analysis, eight of the 13 S&P 500 bear markets overlapped with recessions, as defined by the National Bureau of Economic Research, and five did not. The NBER states a recession is "a significant decline in economic activity that is spread across the economy and lasts more than a few months.".

    The 1973-74 oil shock, the dot-com bust in 2000, the 2007-09 financial crisis and the 2020 pandemic downturn all overlapped with recessions. But some major bear markets also occurred without one, including in 1987 and 2022.

    In a recent development, deutsche Bank macro strategist Henry Allen remarked that every S&P 500 bear market since the 1962 "Kennedy Slide" has coincided with at least one of three factors: a recession, worsening economic data raising recession fears, or a cycle of Federal Reserve rate hikes. None of those are present today, at least so far.

    "Much as last week's selloff was severe, it's worth remembering that it has several differences with many of the other substantial risk-off moves in recent times," the London-based strategist wrote on Tuesday.

    In a recent development, allen noted there hasn't been any sudden reassessment of the growth outlook recently, which happened during the Covid-19 shock, when the pandemic pushed the global economy into recession and the S&P 500 plunged 33.9% in just 33 days. Nor is the current situation similar to the 2025 "Liberation Day" tariff period either, which also prompted a reassessment of the growth outlook.

    Recent findings suggest that economic numbers aren't deteriorating either, with the November U.S. flash composite Purchasing Managers' Index, or PMI, at 54.6, above 50 and indicating that business activity continued to expand. Another factor that often coincides with a recession, Allen said, was a big hawkish shift from the central banks, seen in the 1966 and 2022 bear markets.

    "Today however, the equity declines have not coincided with a hawkish repricing," despite widespread expectations that the central bank is set to raise rates again at its final meeting of the year, on Dec. 9, Allen said.

    Today, markets are pricing fewer Fed rate hikes through September 2027 than they were on Oct. 6, when the S&P 500 set its record, Allen mentioned. "If anything, pricing has shifted slightly dovishly with the equity declines.".

    Over more than six decades since 1962, bear markets have always coincided with at least one of those three circumstances, according to Allen.

    "So it would be unusual to see one today without those" happening too, he said.

    Breaking: Trump demands probe into 'record setting error' after third-quarter GDP data gets massive revision higher

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (559 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".
    • Industry observers note that data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S.
    • Sources indicate that that revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".

    Industry observers note that data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S. economy exhibited much stronger growth for the third quarter than initially estimated, showing that real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate. That was revised upward from the department's advance estimate of 3.4%.

    Sources indicate that that revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, where Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress and multiple governorships.

    "I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated," Trump wrote.

    However, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record. It was the largest revision since the 1.2 percentage point revision seen in the second quarter of 2020.

    On an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990. It also tied four other quarters with a similar 0.9 percentage point difference — and was approximately double the average revision of 0.43 percentage points for all 147 quarters.

    The upward revision shows Trump's policies are "delivering results" that defy expectations, White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC.

    According to recent reports, revisions to U.S. economic numbers are not out of the ordinary. Initial reports count on partial survey data and early estimates. That data is later updated with more survey responses — which sometimes leads to changes from the initial reports.

    Sources indicate that GDP data is revised repeatedly over a five-year period. By the time the final revision is done, the average absolute error from the second release to the final is 1.14 percentage points.

    The advance estimate for Q3 U.S. GDP, which came just days before Election Day in early November, was still better than the figure economists had expected at the time. It also highlighted a significant step-up in growth from the second quarter.

    Because that was a strong showing for the economy, some on Wall Street consider this week's revision to be a confirmation of the economy's recent growth trend.

    Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors said immediately following the release that it "reinforces an increasingly familiar tension" that the economy is "performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes.".

    In a recent development, "The economy isn't merely hanging in there. It continues to demonstrate considerable resilience, with consumers spending, businesses investing and few signs that restrictive monetary policy is creating significant cracks in the broader expansion," the firm's chief investment officer said.

    Recent findings suggest that traders are currently pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's December meeting, according to the CME FedWatch tool. They're also anticipating an additional hike in January.

    — CNBC's Jeff Cox and Fred Imbert contributed reporting.

Jones won five of his eight starts last season as Purdy dealt with a toe injury.

    It has been revealed that like Purdy, Justin Herbert (concussion) will also be out this week after not practicing. The Los Angeles Chargers quarterback was placed in protocol after Sunday's loss to the Newly introduced York Jets.

    "This isn't my first rodeo with regard to starting quarterbacks having an injury you don't know at the beginning of the week when we start game planning," mentioned offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with DJ Uiagalelei set to start for the 1-9 Chargers after Herbert was ruled out.

    Other Week 12 injuries to monitor:.

    In a recent development, parker Washington has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans. The Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver injured his shoulder in practice on Thursday and is considered week-to-week. Running back Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will also not play. Chris Rodriguez Jr. take over as the starter.

    Las Vegas Raiders listed tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) has been listed as questionable after being limited early this week and missing Friday's practice. Bowers missed last week's loss to the Denver Broncos after exiting Week 10 early.

    Recent findings suggest that kirk Cousins won't get one of his weapons back in Week 12 as wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) remains sidelined. Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell mentioned Addison is "progressing well," but he will not be back on the field in Week 12.

    Tee Higgins (hamstring) woke up sore on Friday morning and did not practice for the Cincinnati Bengals. There is no worry there, head coach Zac Taylor mentioned, as he should be fine for the game against the Upcoming Orleans Saints despite the "questionable" designation.

    Carson Beck (back) is ruled out for the second week in a row while dealing with back spasms. Josh Johnson, who started last week in a blowout loss to the Chiefs, will be starting under center for the Arizona Cardinals yet again.

    #166433. AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (970 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.
    • Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.
    • Industry observers note that huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    Industry observers note that huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Sources indicate that huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he mentioned.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    According to recent reports, coreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he stated. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    While Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress said during the company's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he said.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "substantial trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy noted in a note Monday.

    Nvidia noted on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These challenges have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," noted economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    It has been revealed that "The firm is doing everything in its power to execute," he stated. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In a recent development, in the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump stated Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Sources indicate that "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg mentioned. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".

    Steelers WR DK Metcalf appears to shout out Aaron Rodgers via sign language after scoring TD: 'Stand on business 8'

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (339 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In case you somehow haven't heard, Aaron Rodgers was not playing for the Pittsburgh Steelers during their game on Black Friday.
    • Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf, one of Rodgers' closest teammates during his time in Pittsburgh, appeared to shout out the quarterback after scoring a touchdown in the first quarter against the Denver Broncos.
    • The translation via American Sign Language: "Stand on business, eight." Eight was Rodgers' jersey number with the Steelers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In case you somehow haven't heard, Aaron Rodgers was not playing for the Pittsburgh Steelers during their game on Black Friday. That doesn't mean his presence wasn't felt.

    Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf, one of Rodgers' closest teammates during his time in Pittsburgh, appeared to shout out the quarterback after scoring a touchdown in the first quarter against the Denver Broncos. After catching the 22-yard pass from latest starter Mason Rudolph, viewers noted Metcalf making a series of hand signals.

    The translation via American Sign Language: "Stand on business, eight." Eight was Rodgers' jersey number with the Steelers.

    Pittsburgh entered the game carrying some very public baggage, after their starting quarterback burned every bridge in sight on his way out. The Steelers responded with a dominant performance — including two defensive touchdowns in the first half — thumping the Denver Broncos 27-5. Metcalf caught three passes for 36 yards and the touchdown in the win.

    DJ Metcalf caught a touchdown pass from one quarterback then sent a message to another.

    Recent findings suggest that the trouble reportedly began when Rodgers made some sort of "ultimatum," as Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy put it, on Tuesday, which the team did not heed. Instead, Pittsburgh opted to bench Rodgers and start Rudolph against Denver, which led to Rodgers appearing on his friend Pat McAfee's show on ESPN on Wednesday and unleashing a torrent of grievances against McCarthy. The Steelers released Rodgers not long after.

    Even more details were provided during the game Friday, as broadcaster Al Michaels shared the contents of a text from Rodgers, who claimed McCarthy ghosted him until the benching was announced and that the Steelers barred him from the facilities on Wednesday.

    A larger question to come out of the dispute was how the rest of the Steelers players would respond to a dispute between quarterback and head coach. A lopsided win was a decent sign the team wasn't tearing itself apart, but Metcalf's gesture indicates Rodgers still has support from the roster.

    Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
    • Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the upcoming year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    Emery remarked: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    “Of course there is still work to do but they revealed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    Industry observers note that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a massive chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Sources indicate that alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    Industry observers note that PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    According to recent reports, the VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

    Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

    Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

    Recent findings suggest that mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

    In a recent development, other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

    Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

    According to recent reports, two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

    After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

    On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

    Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

    Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

    What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Sources indicate that aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a massive summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    It has been revealed that “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    Industry observers note that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    It has been revealed that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    According to recent reports, PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    #166419. Breaking: Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (993 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (993 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the tech giant's board to rehire Huang.
    • "Clearly they caved to external pressure," said Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-manufacturer director.
    • Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the tech giant's board to rehire Huang. But investigations into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

    "Clearly they caved to external pressure," said Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-manufacturer director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders.".

    Industry observers note that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta remarked on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

    Industry observers note that directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the company and Huang, its co-founder.

    Now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage, who asked not to be named because they are not authorized to speak publicly about client matters, said the tech giant built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

    Nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor said. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.”.

    A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to another industry expert, who has 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named due to sensitivity surrounding relationships with past or potential future clients.

    But Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to the risk advisor. Side A protects directors and officers personally when the firm cannot indemnify them. Side B covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C protects the company when it's named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim.

    The risk advisor indicates Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

    Sources indicate that that choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the company’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

    An insurance CEO, who asked not to be named in order to protect client relationships, characterized a billion-dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but mentioned a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

    That structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to the D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

    "For a company with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," said the industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance.".

    According to recent reports, "It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert stated. The tech giant decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B and Side C are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

    The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the tech giant’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

    A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

    A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the company and Huang misled investors.

    The distinction matters: The derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

    Sources indicate that "Insurance is already at work," remarked Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything.".

    According to recent reports, A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

    The board has already taken steps it claims are aimed at accountability. Nvidia revealed an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia noted it had no reason to believe national security or manufacturer secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

    Recent findings suggest that atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, noted allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a manufacturer’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

    It has been revealed that “Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” stated Atkins, author of "Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value.".

    Nvidia’s 2026 proxy also says the company has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Austin Reaves will return to the Los Angeles Lakers' lineup for their NBA Cup matchup with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday. He is listed as available on the team's injury report.

    According to recent reports, reaves, 28, has been sidelined since suffering a bruised heel in a Nov. 11 win over the Milwaukee Bucks. At the time, the Lakers believed Reaves' injury wasn't serious and didn't require imaging. Head coach JJ Redick said the guard was day-to-day. However, he missed the team's next five games.

    During that five-game span, the Lakers went 4-1 while facing lesser teams including the Charlotte Hornets (4-13), Utah Jazz (3-16) and Sacramento Kings (2-16).

    Recent findings suggest that in 12 games this season, Reaves is averaging 24.7 points per game, second behind Luka Dončić, who leads the league with an average of 36.6 points. He's also averaging 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals while shooting 41% on 66 3-point attempts.

    Recent findings suggest that the Spurs also could get guards De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper back for Friday's game. Both are listed as questionable.

    The Lakers go into Friday's matchup with the NBA's best record at 15-3, a half-game ahead of the 15-4 Spurs.

    In the NBA Cup standings, both teams have a 2-1 record in the Western Conference's Group C. San Antonio would win the group with a win and the Portland Trail Blazers losing to the Golden State Warriors. However, with a +48 point differential, the Spurs could still advance on a tiebreaker.

    According to recent reports, the Lakers would prevail with a victory and a Warriors loss. But a defeat would eliminate them from the in-season tournament.

    #166399. Latest Update: Semiconductor chips are the fresh oil. Here's why

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Semiconductor chips are the fresh oil. Here's why

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.
    • Sources indicate that yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks.
    • Nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.

    Sources indicate that yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks. Last week, before Monday's breathtaking reversal, semiconductor stocks suffered their worst weekly loss in a quarter century, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunging nearly 11% last Friday alone, capping a more than 17% weekly decline.

    Nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch. Then it fell again, dropping almost 10% on Tuesday and Wednesday. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 20% in two days last Thursday and Friday. Micron Technology sank 27% over the seven days ended last Friday.

    Sources indicate that "For decades we've talked about the petrodollar. Perhaps increasingly we need to think about the chip dollar," Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research at Deutsche Bank wrote in a report this month.

    Semiconductor exports overtook oil and gas for the first time during the January-March quarter of 2026, reaching about $1.61 trillion, compared with $1.53 trillion for oil and gas, the report noted, using four-quarter rolling totals.

    The gap widened in the second quarter, when semiconductor exports totaled about $1.60 trillion and oil and gas exports reached about $1.47 trillion. Disruptions to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war helped widen the gap. Daily oil flows through the Strait collapsed nearly 77%, to 4.9 million barrels in the second quarter of 2026 from 21.6 million barrels in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

    Recent findings suggest that yet the demand for semiconductors has proven insatiable in the face of soaring data center construction, boosting global trade in the increasingly scarce AI component. Hundreds of billions of dollars of orders for graphics processing units and data centers aim at providing AI computing power, Rothschild & Co. Redburn wrote in a report last Thursday.

    "Compute will be the fresh commodity fueling this transformation on a global scale," Rothschild analyst Cara Thomson remarked.

    The shift toward chips has macroeconomic implications just as the explosion in oil trade did in the 1970s.

    Oil-exporting countries historically recycled much of their surpluses into the purchase of U.S. Treasuries and other bonds, helping finance U.S. deficits and underpin demand for other government debt.

    It has been revealed that reid at Deutsche Bank remarked that since semiconductor-surplus countries in Asia are more closely tied to U.S. tech companies, some chip-export earnings could flow back into U.S. technology stocks, startups and data centers, further helping to finance the AI investment cycle.

    The changing dynamics in global trade could also tilt the mix of global financial flows, Reid remarked. "So welcome to the chip-dollar era: potentially more growth, more excitement, more volatility, and structurally higher yields" in corporate and government debt.

    Sources indicate that aaron Rodgers made quite a few waves on his way out of the Pittsburgh Steelers organization earlier this week. He had more to say during their first game without him — a game they won 27-5 over the Denver Broncos.

    Sources indicate that prime Video broadcaster Al Michaels relayed a text message he got from the former MVP during the Steelers' game against the Denver Broncos, which attempted to rebut some of his critics and explain why he handled things the way he did.     First, Rodgers complained about the idea he has committed some sort of locker room faux pas by airing out dirty laundry involving Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, whom Rodgers accused of a number of shortcomings during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday:.

    "A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room … The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.".

    That rebuttal could be aimed at a number of notable figures:.

    Rodgers' quarterbacking peer Tom Brady stated, "The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place.".

    Rodgers' former coach Mike Tomlin mentioned it was sad "to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.".

    In a recent development, steelers owner Art Rooney II noted, "In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned.".

    Former Steelers quarterbacks Terry Bradshaw and Russell Wilson both expressed their disapproval.

    Aaron Rodgers still has something to say after the NFL's loudest divorce.

    As for how things played out with the Steelers, it's known that Rodgers made some sort of ultimatum — reportedly that he wanted to call plays on offense or be released — and the Steelers opted to announce his benching late Tuesday night and then release him Wednesday after he aired his grievances against McCarthy.

    Rodgers claimed he got no communication from McCarthy until his benching was announced, and that he only appeared on McAfee's show after the Steelers barred him from their facility:.

    "They took this public, never heard from the head coach, then they leak at 11:00 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to McAfee.".

    Odds are this won't be the last time we hear about Rodgers on this.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, his former teammates defeated the Broncos 27-5 on Friday behind a dominant defensive performance. Rodgers did appear to receive a shout-out from wide receiver DK Metcalf, though.

    #166393. Latest Update: In first game without Aaron Rodgers, Steelers throttle Broncos in blowout win

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1549 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: In first game without Aaron Rodgers, Steelers throttle Broncos in blowout win

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aaron Rodgers' fiery exit seemed to wake up the Pittsburgh Steelers.
    • They benched Rodgers on a Tuesday after 11 p.m.
    • Then the Steelers got to the game Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aaron Rodgers' fiery exit seemed to wake up the Pittsburgh Steelers.

    The Steelers had a wild week. They benched Rodgers on a Tuesday after 11 p.m. The next day Rodgers gave an instantly infamous interview on Pat McAfee's ESPN show, blasting Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, and he was cut shortly after. The entire franchise seemed to be on fire.

    Then the Steelers got to the game Friday. It might have been a short-term boost for a team rallying around its latest starting quarterback Mason Rudolph, its coach or just each other after a week of controversy, but the Steelers played a tremendous game and blew out the Denver Broncos 27-5.

    "I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their [positional player] rooms and it definitely showed up," McCarthy told reporters postgame.

    The Broncos were 8-2 coming in and were outmatched from the first minutes of the game. Rudolph played a solid game, completing 9-of-15 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers' defense kept the Broncos out of the end zone. It was an impressive performance.

    The Steelers are 7-4 and there's a very good chance they'll head to the playoffs. There are still plenty of questions over McCarthy's ability to lead after Rodgers' diatribe over his habits like skipping walkthrough practices and not watching film (and very few denials of Rodgers' claims), and an on-field problem over whether Rudolph can be good enough to make the Steelers much more than blowout fodder in the postseason.

    But for at least one day, the Steelers looked like a brand latest team.

    DK Metcalf of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates with Pat Freiermuth (88) after scoring a touchdown against the Denver Broncos.

    According to recent reports, the Steelers were supposed to be the team in chaos. They looked far more put together than the Broncos.

    Industry observers note that rallying around Rudolph and themselves after a week of controversy, the Steelers had a remarkable first half. A few minutes into the second quarter, after a Broncos punt, the Steelers led 14-0 and had outgained the visiting team 105-8. Even though the Steelers got tackled in the end zone for a safety after that punt, it didn't really slow them down.

    "There's a lot going on. Anytime you're going through a situation where time is taken away from winning and your team responds, it is extremely vital and gratifying," McCarthy remarked. "But the reality of this game … this is a player's game.".

    Late in the first half, Nix continued his awful day. He had already had the ball slip out of his hands for a fumble that was recovered in the end zone by the Steelers, and inside of the two-minute warning he threw a baffling pass. It was hard to tell who Nix was targeting because it went right to cornerback Jalen Ramsey, who returned it 36 yards for a touchdown and a 24-5 lead. There wasn't a Broncos receiver within the vicinity of the pass.

    The Broncos were terrible in the first half. They had 58 yards and didn't score a touchdown, while giving up two to the Steelers' defense. But the Steelers had a lot to do with it. They seemed like a team that was excited to put the drama of the week behind and play football.

    The Steelers just had to sit on the lead in the second half. The Broncos made that easy by not doing much.

    The Broncos couldn't run the ball against a good Steelers front. Nix was really bad. Wil Lutz missed a field goal on the first play of the fourth quarter, and the Amazon broadcast remarked the Broncos let the third quarter run out and therefore Lutz had to kick to the side of the stadium that was tougher on kickers due to weather. That seemed like an unforced error by Broncos head coach Sean Payton. The Broncos' defense played better in the second half, but Pittsburgh's offense seemed to know that the game was in hand and it just had to not screw things up.

    It was a bad performance by the Broncos on a rainy Friday afternoon and perhaps the best one the Steelers have had all season.

    It has been revealed that there were still reminders of Rodgers and the long week Pittsburgh had. After DK Metcalf scored a touchdown he put up four fingers on each hand, perhaps a shoutout to Rodgers, who wore No. 8. During the broadcast, Amazon announcer Al Michaels stated Rodgers texted him and said he was "barred" from the team's facility on Wednesday after his release. It's not like the Rodgers story is going away for the Steelers.

    In a recent development, but winning cures everything. And on Friday, the Steelers looked reborn.

    A slow Denver drive to end the game will seal the deal for Pittsburgh, who picks up a massive 22-point win after days of off-field drama. Mason Rudolph had a very solid start in a time of genuine turmoil, but it's the Steelers defense who really deserves its flowers, getting two of Pittsburgh's touchdowns and forcing three turnovers from quarterback Bo Nix.

    Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is all smiles as he leaves the field, with a well-deserved win through the noise.

    A chant of "F*** you Rodgers" from some Steelers fans is audible on the broadcast. So far, this has been a dominant form of revenge for Pittsburgh after everything that went down with Aaron Rodgers this week.

    Industry observers note that after a false start penalty and a sack, Denver goes for it on fourth-and-21 — which, down 22 points with less than 10 minutes left, is kind of the only option. But Bo Nix's long pass is easily picked off by rookie cornerback Daylen Everette, as the Steelers collect their third forced turnover of the game.

    Jalen Ramsey is flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct on that play, giving the Broncos a 15-yard boost. It's not entirely clear what the flag was for, though Ramsey was nearby as safety Jaquan Brisker appeared make some contact with Pat Bryant after tackling the receiver. The flag may have been intended for Brisker (No. 3) instead of Ramsey (No. 5) — or might be due to an unrelated incident.

    Chris Bowell scores the first points of the second half, with a 33-yarder to grow Pittsburgh's lead to 22 points.

    That's a beautiful pass from Rudolph, who debuts it way downfield to the leaping Wilson for a 37-yard gain.

    Wil Lutz starts the fourth quarter by attempting a 53-yard field goal on fourth-and-17, but the kick goes wide right, likely affected by the wind in the open-air stadium. Tough break for Denver, as things continue going wrong for their offense this half.

    It has been revealed that courtland Sutton is called for offensive pass interference after a shove on an incomplete pass. And on third-and-long, Jalen Ramsey deflects a pass perfectly to force Denver to fourth down again as the third quarter comes to an end.

    This Pittsburgh defense has been really, really fun to watch, even as the score holds in the second half.

    According to recent reports, A weather update: Per Accuweather, it's right now 40 degrees in Pittsburgh, with windchill bringing the temperature down to a feel of 30 degrees. More importantly, it's raining and windy, making gripping the ball and keeping it in the air a bit harder.

    And just like that, a promising Pittsburgh drive abruptly comes to an end, with Rico Dowdle losing the ball and the Broncos recovering.

    Denver catches a break, and sets up a chance to try and get some second-half points on the board.

    Dowdle converts on third-and-2 with a well-blocked 8-yard gain, before following up with a 27-yard rush to put the Steelers over the midline.

    A promising Broncos drive again ends in a punt, after Bo Nix's pass attempt for Pat Bryant on third down is nearly picked off before falling short.

    In a recent development, after moving the chains with a 22-yard throw to Jaylen Waddle, Bo Nix finds the space with his feet this time, sprinting on third-and-7 to slide across the first-down line. Good movement from Nix so far this drive.

    We have a first down conversion! Denver gets the ball to Jonah Coleman on seocnd-and-1, and the tenacious running back pushes through for a two-yard gain to move the chains. Finally, we will have a drive in this half last longer than three plays.

    Steelers have to punt as well. Four straight three-and-outs between the two teams to start this half.

    According to recent reports, the Broncos and Steelers are trading three-and-outs to start the second half: Denver is forced to punt for the second time this half, and Pittsburgh will get the ball again while hoping to make something of it. Strong start for both defenses…and less so on the offensive end.

    Industry observers note that the Broncos go three-and-out again to start off the second half, after another pair of incomplete passes from Bo Nix. The Steelers are not letting up on defense, with some more excellent pass coverage to break things up.

    According to recent reports, second half is underway! Denver will get the ball first to try and spark a comeback.

    • Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.
    • Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

    Published: 18:28 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:19 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

    Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

    Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

    Neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'.

    According to recent reports, emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

    It has been revealed that an interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he remarked: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

    Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds.

    On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram.

    He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club.

    Industry observers note that 'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'.

    It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

    Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.
    • That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it.
    • As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Playing for the G League Westchester Knicks, former NBA first-round pick Rob Dillingham was involved in a scuffle during Friday's matchup with the Capital City Go-Go.
    • In the fourth quarter of Westchester's 125-104 win, Dillingham was punched by Capital City center Felix Okpara at the top of the 3-point line.
    • When one wasn't made, Okpara clotheslined Dillingham across the neck and shoulders, knocking him to the floor.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Playing for the G League Westchester Knicks, former NBA first-round pick Rob Dillingham was involved in a scuffle during Friday's matchup with the Capital City Go-Go.

    In the fourth quarter of Westchester's 125-104 win, Dillingham was punched by Capital City center Felix Okpara at the top of the 3-point line. Dillingham pushed Okpara on his way down the court, and the center looked at the official for a foul call.

    When one wasn't made, Okpara clotheslined Dillingham across the neck and shoulders, knocking him to the floor.

    Sources indicate that both teams then gathered in a scrum past the Westchester basket, going off the court as Okpara backpedaled toward the baseline. Coaches, officials and arena security personnel then separated each group of players.

    Ermal Kuqo, the Knicks' senior director of minor league operations, and his 6-foot-10, 270-pound frame also got involved, which surely helped provide a significant obstacle to fisticuffs.

    Dillingham and Okpara were subsequently both ejected from the game. Dillingham finished with 10 points and 8 assists, while Okpara scored 12 points with 9 rebounds for the Go-Go.

    Okpara was the Washington Wizards' second-round pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, selected No. 46 overall out of Tennessee. In three games with the Wizards, he averaged one point and 0.7 rebounds in five minutes of play. In the G League, Okpara is scoring 11.4 points, 8.8 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game.

    Dillingham was the San Antonio Spurs' 2024 first-round pick, selected No. 8 overall out of Kentucky. He was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves on draft night for a first-round pick swap in 2030 and first-rounder in 2031.

    In a recent development, last season, the T-Wolves dealt him midway through his second season in a trade involving Ayo Dosunmu going to the Chicago Bulls. Before training camp this season, he was moved to the Charlotte Hornets in exchange for Buddy Hield but was subsequently waived. In November, he signed with the Latest York Knicks' G League team.

    In three games with Westchester, Dillingham is averaging 21 points and 6.3 assists per game while shooting 35% on 17 3-point attempts.
