    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • Industry observers note that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    Industry observers note that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below.

    The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set new records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    Industry observers note that 3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    Sources indicate that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.

    Sources indicate that the Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.

    According to recent reports, acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs.

    It has been revealed that the Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The newly introduced extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    In a recent development, melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.

    In a recent development, the New York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.

    According to recent reports, loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.

    New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:.

    Industry observers note that "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting.".

    In a recent development, the 23-year-old Domínguez still has big-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.

    Industry observers note that lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the Upcoming York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.

    It has been revealed that the Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.

    Recent findings suggest that the Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.

    It has been revealed that the New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.

    According to recent reports, hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

    Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
    • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
    • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes demonstrated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    According to recent reports, devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they revealed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

    Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

    Recent findings suggest that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

    Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

    The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

    Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

    Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

    Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 5.

    Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

    Leeds United 4 Manchester United 3.

    Top right. Sudden death now effectively.

    Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

    Rolls it casually past the right post.

    Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

    Leeds United 2 Manchester United 3.

    Leeds United 2 Manchester United 2.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 2.

    Bottom right. Took it very quickly.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

    Smacks it even higher into the top right.

    Leeds United 1 Manchester United 0.

    So there will be another short delay.

    And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

    The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

    It has been revealed that not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

    Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

    In a recent development, two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

    It’s like Euro 2016 all over again.

    Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

    Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

    According to recent reports, cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

    Sources indicate that enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

    Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

    The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

    Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

    Sources indicate that there will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

    Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

    Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

    Sources indicate that clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

    In a recent development, jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

    It has been revealed that yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

    In a recent development, understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

    Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

    Industry observers note that dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

    Industry observers note that zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

    Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

    According to recent reports, just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

    Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

    Lammens saves from Harry Wilson’s shot from 10 yards after Rodon’s underlapping ran down the right caught Amass off guard.

It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    According to recent reports, this one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That crucial date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    Most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    All that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    It has been revealed that the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder issue this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a newly introduced team before Opening Day.

    According to recent reports, as a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout challenges. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    It has been revealed that on the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    In a recent development, the Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 major-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    Recent findings suggest that A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028. Raley's power against righties and an extra year of control could make him a solid bench option moving forward.

    Recent findings suggest that you can't make the playoffs in 10 games, but you can definitely give yourself some breathing room when the inevitable ebbs and flows of the season strike. That's exactly what the Boston Bruins have done as they've stood out for the right reasons in a deep Atlantic Division.

    Boston right now leads the division with 15 points, and while the Tampa Bay Lightning's record is technically better, the Bruins' plus-14 goal differential is tied for second in the NHL.

    In a recent development, the biggest reason for this fast start has been the play of Jeremy Swayman in goal. He's allowed one or fewer goals in half of his starts, and Swayman's 8.02 goals saved above average ranks second to old Beantown running mate Linus Ullmark, per Natural Stat Trick.

    We have a long way to go before we start discussing Vezina Trophy candidates seriously, but Swayman certainly has the potential to carry Boston to the postseason.

    Recent findings suggest that it helps that David Pastrnak is an elite playmaker, and the Bruins have been getting contributions from young forwards Fraser Minten and James Hagens. Morgan Geekie has also gone from goal-scoring machine to distributor with seven assists in 10 games.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atlantic Division will be a heavyweight brawl throughout the season, but to this point, the Bruins have proven to be a worthy combatant. With that in mind, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    • Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026.
    • Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.
    • The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 05:59 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:11 EST, 23 November 2026.

    Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live interview immediately after winning a trophy with his Boca Juniors side.

    The 32-year-old was one of the focal points of a World Cup side that reached the final last summer, and went on to win the Copa Sudamericana on Saturday evening after beating Brazil's Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in Barranquilla.

    But amid the thick humidity and Colombian heat, Paredes became overwhelmed moments after lifting the trophy.

    After giving a brief interview, Paredes was captured closing his eyes, before falling towards the interviewer, who attempted to break his fall.

    Instead, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder hit the ground, with attendants rushing to help him after his collapse.

    Paredes had been taken off in the second-half after suffering from heat-related dizziness, with humidity at 80 per cent heading into the match, and 32-degree-temperatures.

    Leandro Parades collapsed to the floor during a post-match interview after winning the Copa Sudamericana with Boca Juniors.

    The interviewer attempted to break his fall as the former PSG crumpled to the turf.

    'He felt dizzy towards the end of the first-half,' his manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena explained of the substitution. 'He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second-half, you could see he was struggling.'.

    Fortunately, Paredes was revived rapidly and treated in the treatment room, before re-joining his team's celebrations after claiming the South American trophy.

    The star shared a brief statement on social media confirming he was fine after the interview aired.

    'We're fine,' Paredes confirmed with a picture taken during treatment, before adding in a separate caption: 'Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just a dizziness from so many turns together'.

    Paredes' triumph for his club side comes months after agonising defeat to Spain in Latest York at the World Cup final in July.

    Argentina were felled by a solitary goal from Ferran Torres to end their reign as world champions, before the match descended into petty scraps - with Paredes at the heart of the bad behaviour.

    Paredes furiously shoved Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle blew, earning himself a punchy 10-match suspension from FIFA.

    He faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two, and both players were also fined $90,000 (£66,000).

    Paredes himself admitted that the length of the ban had put his international future under consideration.

    Recent findings suggest that 'It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,' Paredes told the media in September. 'Because of the suspension as well, because of (Lionel Messi) Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

    'I haven't discussed it with the coach (Lionel Scaloni) yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make.'.

    Paredes' announcement came just days after Messi decided to hang up his international boots, with the talismanic Argentina superstar treated to a magnificent send-off during the early Autumn international break.

    'Leo's legacy will live on forever because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled,' Paredes added.

    Paredes updated fans after the incident to confirm he was okay before rejoining the festivities with his team-mates (Source: Instagram/Leandro Parades).

    'We'd spoken in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even so, we weren't prepared for that because of what he means to us.'.

    Although unable to compete alongside him in their country's colours for one last time, Paredes joined Messi on the pitch in Buenos Aires for his final farewell, and shared an emotional tribute post to his former captain.

    'THANK YOU FOR ABSOLUTELY EVERYTHING CAPTAIN,' he captioned a carousel of photos of himself and Messi.

    'It was a dream to be able to have achieved everything we achieved together and to have defended this shirt and our country with you, I'm leaving and we'll miss you always.

    According to recent reports, 'It was a pleasure to be one of your soldiers for all these years and I will be forever! I love you buddy.'.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan released himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?
    • The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining.
    • Sources indicate that officially, it will count as dunk No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan released himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    Let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    Did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Sources indicate that officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    That begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    According to recent reports, wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    Fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he remarked after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    Industry observers note that if he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

    Recent findings suggest that for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Industry observers note that goaltending has been an issue in Latest Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    According to recent reports, in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Newly introduced Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    In a recent development, hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    It has been revealed that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    It has been revealed that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    It has been revealed that let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Industry observers note that that noted, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Industry observers note that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Recent findings suggest that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    Sources indicate that the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason.
    • Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal.
    • Sources indicate that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason. Sure enough, they are "listening to trade offers" for All-Star starting pitcher Logan Webb, per The Athletic, but they'd need a "very strong return" in order to deal him.

    Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal. He went 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.3 WAR last season, but it was his worst year in quite a while. He averaged 4.5 WAR per season in the previous four years with a 3.22 ERA and led the National League in innings pitched from 2023 to 2025, racking up three straight top-six Cy Young finishes.

    Sources indicate that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb? Many of them. We're talking about a workhorse under team control for two more years. Let's run through five of the best fits while, again, knowing that basically any contender should be interested in at least a conversation with the Giants.

    It has been revealed that the Cubs need so much pitching this offseason. Their entire rotation heading into the playoffs last season is in free agency. This isn't hyperbole. Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson are all off the roster. If the Cubs were to try and put together a rotation right now, it would be something like Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and several question marks. Ben Brown and Cade Horton will open the season on the injured list.

    According to recent reports, do we really need to spell out what a reliable innings eater would mean for this bunch? Webb is an outstanding fit here.

    Recent findings suggest that the upstart playoff team last season was a ton of fun, but also was running bullpen games in the ALDS. The White Sox just attached Davis Martin to Luis Castillo in a trade to the Rockies in order to offload Castillo's contract, too, so they're down a starter. The Dustin May signing means they have him along with Sean Burke and converted reliever Grant Taylor. The White Sox would reportedly like to sign another starter in the May ballpark, but what about trading for someone better like Webb?

    A top four in the rotation of Webb, Burke, Taylor and May would be exponentially better than what the Sox had last season.

    Returns of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach at some point will help, but this is still a thin rotation for a team coming off a division title. Chris Sale remains, but he's followed up with Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder before the Spencers return. Youngster Didier Fuentes moving to the rotation is exciting, but there are an awful lot of questions behind Sale, who turns 38 in late March, by the way.

    Recent findings suggest that given that the Padres reside in the NL West with the Giants, there might be a bit of an intradivision tax in terms of the asking price, but Padres boss A.J. Preller is never shy about offloading prospects. There could certainly be a fit. The Padres need rotation help, too, after losing Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and others to free agency. We know they're in on Tarik Skubal, but that doesn't mean they'll be content with just landing one substantial fish.

    Sources indicate that look at the current Padres rotation. It's basically Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez. With three straight playoff berths and zero trips to the World Series, now isn't the time to have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig make up 60% of the rotation.

    Dealing for Webb and signing Skubal would make for a nice offseason for new ownership, no?

    Industry observers note that one of the most disappointing teams in baseball last season needs to have a prolific offseason. We've heard plenty about the Mets being involved in the Skubal sweepstakes and we've seen them win a monster bidding war before (see: Soto, Juan). Grabbing Webb would make it quite a well-rounded rotation with talented youngsters Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.

    Damian Lillard stars in his Milwaukee return in another stark reminder of how bleak things are for the Bucks

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up!
    • Bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
    • In a recent development, lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

    Bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

    In a recent development, lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

    Sources indicate that trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he said, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

    Lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard stated.

    No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

    It has been revealed that "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori noted pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

    The moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

    The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

    "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard remarked Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

    Recent findings suggest that the desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

    Five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

    Sources indicate that and the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

    No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

    Recent findings suggest that just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a latest promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

    Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case.

    We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there.

    Industry observers note that tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and stated that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers").

    The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

    The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

    The Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

    Industry observers note that gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

    The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

    The Red Sox also reportedly demonstrated interest.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year. The Grizzlies were a popular pick to surprise some folks this year, but nobody saw this coming. On the other hand, Luka Dončić and Victor Wembanyama are lording over the league like castles on a hill, and that wasn't so hard to predict.

    It has been revealed that and then there's been everything in between. All the injuries, perhaps most notably. The Raptors and Pacers entered the season being hyped as new-look contenders, but so far Tyrese Haliburton and Kawhi Leonard have combined to play six games. The Warriors went from an eight-game winning streak to the Washington Generals with one Stephen Curry abdominal tweak. The 76ers can't lose a clutch game in a maze. Paul George has been reborn in Boston. The Rockets are flying. The Heat are getting hot. The Knicks' fog is lifting. It feels like Damian Lillard never left the Blazers. This rookie class looks potentially historic.

    So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware. Who's been the MVP so far? What about the best rookie? What has been the biggest surprise? Biggest disappointment? In light of what we've seen so far, is anyone ready to change their preseason Finals pick? Our staff took a collective shot at tackling these topics below.

    Sources indicate that botkin: It's a two-horse race so far and nobody is going to argue much with either pick, but I'm going with Luka. I thought the Lakers would be good (their over/under 46.5 win total was way too low), but not tied-for-the-best-record-in-the-league good. Likewise, we all knew Luka would score huge, but not damn-near 40 PPG huge. Throw in north of seven assists and seven rebounds and almost two steals a night, and the numbers are simply too overwhelming to deny.

    Gonzalez: This is really tough. Luka Dončić has been playing some of the best basketball of his career, and he's a huge reason why the Lakers are down as my big surprise over the first month of the season. But for as good as Luka has been, Wemby's two-way dominance gives him the edge here. Wembanyama had the second 50-point game of his career against the Mavs, and he's averaging a 28-point double-double on 53% shooting from the field. He's also blocking an outrageous 4.1 shots per game and averaging more than a steal per outing. There's no answer for him at either end of the floor.

    Sources indicate that kalland: Wemby's been awesome but for the first month it's gotta be Luka. He's averaging 38 points per game on 47/38/86 splits! The Lakers are 13-3 in spite of defensive concerns, and it's because Dončić is out of his mind. What's amazing is he's going to have to keep up this ridiculous pace to win MVP and for the Lakers to remain at the top of the West. I'm excited to see how long he can maintain this level.

    Maloney: I won't argue with anyone who picks Luka Dončić when he's averaging nearly 40 points per game, but I'm going with Wembanyama because of his two-way dominance. He's third in scoring, fourth in rebounding and first in blocks by a significant margin. The 1.7 blocks-per-game gap between Wembanyama (3.9) and Donovan Clingan (2.2), who sits in second, is as massive as the gap between Clingan and Dean Wade (0.5), who ranks 102nd in the league. In 483 minutes with Wembanyama on the floor this season, the Spurs have a 98.7 defensive rating; in 290 minutes without him, they have a 123.4 defensive rating. Overall, Wembanyama has an unfathomable +41.5 net rating differential.

    Quinn: Dončić is flirting with 40 points per game. He's leading the NBA in both 3-point attempts and free throws. He's the undisputed engine of the NBA's best offense, one that dies whenever he rests. The Lakers have the NBA's best record because Luka Dončić is on their team. That's it. They're average at basically everything else: rebounding, defense, you name it. But their offense dominates because he is on their team. Victor Wembanyama has much more to work with around him. No one else is even in their galaxy, though Stephen Curry might've had a case had he stayed healthy.

    It has been revealed that salerno: I've been pleasantly surprised with the Lakers so far. The pieces are working together nicely. However, the Lakers obviously wouldn't obvousuly be this good without Dončić, who is somehow taking his game to an entirely new level. He's on a mission to win MVP. He's been the best player in the league for the first month of the season. I think this will be the year he finally wins the award.

    Botkin: I actually think Darius Acuff's numbers are actually too good in the sense that voters can't fathom a rookie averaging 26 and 7 without it being some fishy gimmick. It's not a gimmick. He just has total control of an NBA offense, which would make any player's numbers go up, Luka Dončić included. That stated, Lendeborg has been better as both a real go-to player on a real team and from a scoring efficiency standpoint. The honeymoon has been heavily interrupted with Stephen Curry's injury as the Warriors look, well, like the Kings. But as of now Lendeborg deserves the award. Long term, I'm really watching Darryn Peterson as Utah's season rapidly circles the drain. His numbers are rising quickly, and it may not be long before his development becomes Utah's undisputed top priority.

    Recent findings suggest that gonzalez: Lendeborg picked a fight with Luka in his very first game as a pro, trash-talked while guarding the Lakers superstar, then stated he lost all respect for him afterward. He stepped into the starting lineup and immediately looked like he belonged for an injury-plagued Warriors team that sorely needed his presence. And he was so unnerved by a blowout loss to the Spurs that he chopped off his hair, leaving Steve Kerr to tell the media "apparently that's his response to getting beat by 40, is to go right to the barber." His personality alone wins him the award. The numbers are good, too.

    According to recent reports, kalland: This rookie class has lived up to the hype so far, but right now I have to give the edge to the Warriors rookie sensation. Lendeborg came into the league talking that talk, and while he's put his foot in his mouth here and there, he's largely walked the walk to back it up. What separates him from the likes of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer right now is his combination of productivity and efficiency. But we've already seen that take a dip without Stephen Curry so there is certainly an opportunity for others to make up ground as the Warriors struggle without their top star.

    Sources indicate that maloney: Lendeborg has started to fade a bit, and so have the Warriors since Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury, but the No. 11 pick has still done enough to earn the nod ahead of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer. Everyone liked the Lendeborg pick for the Warriors, but no one expected this. He's come in and immediately established himself as their second-best player while doing a little bit of everything. He's second among rookies in scoring, second in rebounding, fifth in assists and tied for fourth in steals, all while shooting 37.2% from 3-point range.

    Quinn: Cameron Boozer is probably trending toward winning. His 3-point shooting is coming around, his interior scoring is progressing, and he does all of the little things everyone promised. Darius Acuff has the biggest numbers, but they're fake. Not fake in the empty calories sense, but fake in that all of the other rookies are being asked to play roles on real basketball teams, whereas Sacramento has elected to devote its entire season to Acuff's development by letting him do basically whatever he wants. If we're simply naming the best rookie thus far this season, though, the answer is obviously Yaxel Lendeborg. Things have gotten harder with Stephen Curry sidelined, but Lendeborg has resuscitated Golden State's postseason ambitions. He's scoring efficiently, shouldering an enormous defensive load and has fit into a system that is notoriously tricky for the wrong kinds of players. Boozer may get there by the end of the season, but for now, this is Yaxel's trophy.

However, I would give strong consideration to Acuff because he is being asked to do more than any other rookie in his class. He is putting up elite numbers on a very bad Kings team that would be even worse if he wasn't in the lineup. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the top contenders. Darryn Peterson has also played very well as of late and will end up being in the mix down the stretch.

    According to recent reports, botkin: So many good options here. Obviously the Grizzlies, who are probably the correct answer. I certainly didn't foresee Minnesota holding this tightly to the rope without Anthony Edwards. But I'm going with the 76ers, who felt like a team that was going to take a while to figure things out but instead are out to a 13-3 record. There are some qualifiers. A perfect 11-0 mark in clutch games is unsustainable, and they can't keep digging themselves into holes (six comeback wins from at least 10 down). But the bottom line is this is a team that looks like it has played together for far longer than it has. The roles clarified almost immediately. Joel Embiid hasn't gotten hurt yet. There's a mental toughness to this team that I suppose makes sense given the individual players we're talking about, but collectively this thing is way more tied together than I thought possible this early in the season.

    Industry observers note that gonzalez: There weren't many people outside of Los Angeles who predicted the Lakers would be atop the Western Conference a month into the season. There might not have been that many inside Los Angeles either. The skepticism can be forgiven considering the Lakers bid goodbye to arguably the greatest player of all time during the summer, then overhauled a large portion of the roster. In came Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Matisse Thybulle, among others. After the reconstruction, head coach JJ Redick remarked that for the first time in his tenure "the pieces actually fit together." That's been the case so far on the offensive end. The Lakers are first in points per game and third in offensive rating. It definitely helps that Luka Dončić is playing some of the best basketball of his career and leading the league in scoring by a wide margin. While Dončić battles Victor Wembanyama for MVP frontrunner status, his Lakers are in a race with the Spurs for the top slot in the West. The former isn't much of a surprise, but the latter certainly is.

    Recent findings suggest that kalland: Yes, the Grizzlies have faced a very generous schedule through the first month of the season, but even with that context, no one predicted a 12-4 start with Ty Jerome hanging out among the league's leading scorers. Cam Boozer's a strong ROY candidate (and is slowly improving his shooting efficiency) and the Grizzlies just keep finding diamonds in the rough to maintain competitiveness. They've got eight guys averaging 10+ points per game and are top 10 in offensive and defensive rating. Reality may arrive soon, but even so, this hot start has given them a great chance at emerging as a Play-In squad in the West.

    In a recent development, maloney: The NBA intellegencia was high on the Grizzlies coming into the season, but in the sense that they would surpass their win total projection and make a run at the Play-In Tournament. Instead, they've jumped out to a 12-4 start, which has them in fourth place in the Western Conference and is good for the fifth-best record in the league. They lead the league in offensive rating (121.2) and are third in net rating (+9.9) behind only the Spurs and the Celtics. Even though they've had the easiest schedule in the league thus far, this is still remarkable.

Then their best player got hurt ... and they became the NBA's best defense. They're hardly slouching as scorers either. LaMelo Ball's playmaking has facilitated breakout years for Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu. Jonathan Kuminga is making 3s and defending like the Warriors always wanted him to. Minnesota's transition from moodiness to giddiness is palpable whenever they play, and when they get Edwards back, they're going to be terrifying.

Between Boozer being firmly in the Rookie of the Year race and Ty Jerome making a case as the Most Improved Player, the Grizzlies have been quite entertaining to watch. Memphis has pushed the right buttons.

    It has been revealed that botkin: I'm probably a little biased on this one. I'm a lifelong Warriors fan and figured they would stink this year, but I allowed myself to get my hopes up with the way the team came out of the gate. I should've known better. As soon as Curry went down, which was probably inevitable, the Warriors turned into one of the worst teams in the league. It's a complete bummer. Hopefully he won't be out too much longer, and the Warriors can pick back up where he left off, but this is just a harsh reminder of how thin the margin is for this team, and it's just not likely to go their way over the long haul. If I was born in Indiana, I would say the same thing about Tyrese Haliburton's injury. Same goes for the Toronto fans with Kawhi only managing two games so far. All the injuries stink. But Curry's has hit the hardest.

    Recent findings suggest that gonzalez: Moving to the 3-2-1 system was unnecessary. The league overcorrected for last year's perfect tanking storm and didn't account for a simple truth of basketball: sometimes teams are just bad. No amount of tinkering is going to stop that. More than half the teams in the East are under .500. The West has four more such teams, bringing the total league-wide to 12. Adam Silver didn't want to incentivize tanking, but by putting too much of the league's thumb on the scale, they've made it harder on the worst teams to get better. Not to mention that the odd entertainment value of fans checking their lottery odds in the tank wars sideshow has been somewhat stripped away. [Stands up and repeats himself yet again] Tanking wasn't actually a problem.

    Kalland: The injuries so far this season have been brutal. Just about every team you'd point to as a disappointment -- Utah, Indiana, Toronto -- can point to injuries as a major reason for their early struggles. The frustrating thing is there's not an easy solve to the injury matter (schedule length is hard to blame for injuries in the first month) and every year it feels like we're playing injury roulette to determine who can and can't be a contender. The wheel started spinning earlier than usual in 2026-27.

    Maloney: I'm going with Robby here. The absurd amount of injuries, coupled with who is getting injured, has been the story of the season so far. You could form an All-Star team with all of the guys who have gone down with multi-week ailments: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Paolo Banchero, Kawhi Leonard, Stephen Curry, Austin Reaves, Dylan Harper, Jalen Duren, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kon Knueppel, Ja Morant, Caleb Wilson, Cason Wallace.

    Quinn: Look, we knew Charlotte was taking a step back when the team traded LaMelo Ball. The Hornets have been plagued by injuries all season. Some of this can be explained. Fine. Their offense still makes me want to vomit. No team turns the ball over more often. No team shoots less efficiently. No team is forced to take more shots in the last four seconds of the shot clock. No team leaves you feeling as though you're watching a panicked 14-year-old try to play minutes for the varsity squad more often. I had very high hopes for No. 1 option Brandon Miller. I trusted the system Charles Lee built last season. I figured they'd be worse, but still respectable, because this organization has displayed a genuine, systemic competence over the past few years. I think that will win out in the end. For now, I pity the poor souls in Charlotte buying tickets to these games, because they're quite nearly unwatchable.

    Salerno: Yes, Utah has been bad this season, largely due to the injury bug, but I was bullish on this team heading into the season. I had Utah finishing sixth in the West and making the playoffs outright. Instead, Utah is heading toward the lottery again, where it doesn't even own its own first-round pick in what should end up being a lackluster draft. The organization's top priority for the remainder of the season is developing Darryn Peterson.

    Botkin: Spurs over Knicks. The Spurs are the clear Western Conference favorite with all the OKC injuries. The Wolves, Lakers and Rockets deserve to be in the conversation, but they're all second-paragraph entries. It's the Spurs until they get hit with some major injury, too, but let's not jinx it. In the East, I could make a case for four teams. The 76ers have the late-game goods and individual creation that is exponentially impactful in the postseason. The Celtics look incredible with Paul George flourishing. The Pistons are just flat-out tough and they've been doing it without Jalen Duren. But I'm still picking the Knicks, who are starting to come out of their fog. They are so perfectly built for the playoffs, and remember, they weren't a great regular-season team last year, either.

    Industry observers note that gonzalez: Spurs over Celtics. After losing their first two games to start the season, the Spurs look every bit as good as they did during last season's run to the finals -- if not better. The three-guard starting unit hasn't slowed them down at all, and Wemby has been unreal at both ends of the floor. And while the Celtics took a lot of heat in the immediate aftermath of the Jaylen Brown for Paul George trade, we all should have known that they would still be among the best teams in the East this season. Both franchises are smart and steady. Meeting this summer would make for an excellent Finals.

    Kalland: Spurs over Celtics. I have to stick with my preseason Finals prediction because it's not every year a preseason pick still looks that good a month in. The Spurs look like a juggernaut, and their top competitor in the West, the OKC Thunder, will once again (likely) be without Jalen Williams for the playoffs. We'll see what the Timberwolves look like when Anthony Edwards returns, but for now it still feels like San Antonio and everyone else. In the East, I felt good about this Celtics team entering the season, and nothing has changed my belief they have what it takes to win the conference.

    Maloney: Spurs over Celtics. I picked Thunder over Celtics ahead of the season, in large part because of how difficult it has been for teams to get back to the Finals in consecutive seasons during this parity era. But now that the Thunder have been decimated with injuries, the Spurs have what appears to be a clear path through the West. I'll stick with the Celtics in the East, which has not been anywhere near as good as we expected this season.

    According to recent reports, quinn: Spurs over Knicks. Oklahoma City's injuries are really all that's changed to me. I don't think the Lakers have the defense or frontcourt depth to win three straight series in the West. I don't think the Rockets will be able to create good enough shots. I need to see Ball prove it in a playoff setting before I trust Minnesota. The star-studded 76ers have thus far been clutch merchants. The underlying numbers are lower on them than their record suggests. The opposite is true for Boston, who is blowing everyone out of the gym, but is going to have complications creating shots off of the dribble in the playoffs and defending man-to-man against the best offenses. I have an eyebrow quirked at Indiana and Toronto when they get their best players back. I'll reengage with the Thunder if and when they cash in some of their trade chips. For now, though, nothing has convinced me that last year's finalists are going to be dethroned. The Knicks and Spurs are the most complete teams in their respective conferences, and I'd expect San Antonio to learn from last June's defeat in a revenge series this time around.

I had the Thunder beating the 76ers in my preseason prediction, but I'm not sure OKC has enough firepower to make a deep run given their injuries. Minnesota is staying afloat even though Anthony Edwards is set to miss more time. LaMelo Ball has been fantastic this season. When Edwards gets back, I'm excited to see them play again. As for the East, it's really a toss-up to say who will make it out of the conference. Boston has been great. Detroit is playing good basketball. The Knicks and Heat are looking better.
